channel.name: MindLoop
channel.promise: One uncomfortable truth about how people work, every day, in under a minute.
channel.audience: 18-34, English-speaking, scrolls Shorts late at night, likes feeling smarter after 45 seconds
channel.voiceOfChannel: Calm, certain, slightly clinical. Never hypey. Never says 'guys'. States the finding, then hands the viewer a use for it.
forbidden: claims about a named real person's psychology
therapy-speak buzzwords (trauma, narcissist, gaslighting) used loosely
clickbait that the video does not pay off

aiDisclosure.note: Voice is synthetic but no realistic synthetic depiction of real people/events is used, so YouTube's 'altered content' disclosure is not required. Re-evaluate if you switch to AI video of realistic humans.

variation.comment: YouTube demonetises 'inauthentic content': templated videos reproduced at scale with no real authorial input. The rotation below is the countermeasure - consecutive uploads must differ in structure, visual language and pacing, not just in topic.

formats.label: The mechanism
formats.structure: Name a behaviour the viewer has seen -> reveal the hidden mechanism driving it -> name the mechanism -> one line the viewer can use tomorrow.
formats.hookPattern: observation the viewer has personally witnessed
formats.visualStyle: real people in ordinary settings, documentary stock footage, handheld feel, cool desaturated grade

formats.label: The study
formats.structure: Set up a real experimental design in one line -> what researchers expected -> what actually happened -> what it means for the viewer.
formats.hookPattern: a setup so strange the viewer needs the result
formats.visualStyle: clinical, archival, muted institutional interiors, paper, corridors, single-subject portraits

formats.label: The inversion
formats.structure: State the advice everyone repeats -> show why it backfires -> give the inverted rule -> the one situation where the original advice does hold.
formats.hookPattern: a belief the viewer holds, stated as if you agree, then broken
formats.visualStyle: clean minimal, negative space, single objects, high contrast, warm key light

formats.label: The field guide
formats.structure: Promise the viewer will be able to spot something -> give 3 concrete tells, each with a visual -> the tell that means you should walk away.
formats.hookPattern: a promise of a new perception the viewer keeps forever
formats.visualStyle: observational close-ups of hands, faces, doorways, screens; shallow depth of field

formats.label: The escalation
formats.structure: Start with a trivially small version of a behaviour -> escalate through 3 steps to its extreme consequence -> land on where the viewer already is on that ladder.
formats.hookPattern: something the viewer does daily, framed as step one of something larger
formats.visualStyle: moody, dark, escalating scale - rooms to streets to crowds to cities, night footage

formats.label: The self-test
formats.structure: Pose a question the viewer answers in their head -> reveal what each answer indicates -> explain the split -> tell them what to do with the answer they gave.
formats.hookPattern: a direct second-person question with only two plausible answers
formats.visualStyle: graphic and typographic, bold colour fields, abstract shapes, almost no footage of people
